set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.

glabel bcpyx_mask
    addiu	$sp, $sp, -184
    sw	$ra, 20($sp)
    sw	$a0, 184($sp)
    lui	$a1, %hi(gS1)

    addiu	$a0, $sp, 56
    jal	memcpy
    li	$a2, 64
    lui	$v0, %hi(gA)
    addiu	$v0, $v0, %lo(gA)
    lw	$a0, 0($v0)
    lw	$a1, 4($v0)
    lw	$a2, 8($v0)
    lw	$a3, 12($v0)

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
void *memcpy(void *, const void *, unsigned long);
extern const u8 gS1[64];
extern const u8 gS2[64];
extern u32 gA[16];
void sink(u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d);

u32 bcpyx_mask(u32 i);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target mips-ido-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function bcpyx_mask   # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

    j	.L48
    sw	$a2, %lo(gHit)($at)

# Reproduce asmlift on `brk2out_ctl` — benchmark function synthetic:brk2out_ctl:gcc2.7.2.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# gcc2.7.2's canonical flags.

# Reproduce asmlift on `brk2out_sw` — benchmark function synthetic:brk2out_sw:gcc2.7.2.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `brk2out_sw` — benchmark function synthetic:brk2out_sw:ido7.1.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile

# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# ido7.1's canonical flags.

# Reproduce m2c on `bvqg` — benchmark function synthetic:bvqg:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel bvqg
    stwu    r1,-16(r1)
    mflr    r0
    stw     r0,20(r1)
    addi    r4,r1,8
    lwz     r5,gQ@sda21(r13)
    lwz     r0,gQ@sda21(r13)
    stw     r5,8(r1)
    stw     r0,12(r1)
    bl       takeQ
    lwz     r0,20(r1)
    mtlr    r0
    addi    r1,r1,16
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
struct W { u32 x; };
struct Q { u32 a, b; };
struct T { u32 a, b, c; };
struct C { u8 b[4]; };
void takeW(struct W w);
void takeQ(s32 k, struct Q q);
void takeT(struct T t);
void takeC(struct C c);
void bvqg(s32 k);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function bvqg         # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `bvqp` — benchmark function synthetic:bvqp:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel bvqp
    stwu    r1,-16(r1)
    mflr    r0
    stw     r0,20(r1)
    lwz     r5,0(r4)
    lwz     r0,4(r4)
    addi    r4,r1,8
    stw     r5,8(r1)
    stw     r0,12(r1)
    bl       takeQ
    lwz     r0,20(r1)
    mtlr    r0
    addi    r1,r1,16
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
struct W { u32 x; };
struct Q { u32 a, b; };
struct T { u32 a, b, c; };
struct C { u8 b[4]; };
void takeW(struct W w);
void takeQ(s32 k, struct Q q);
void takeT(struct T t);
void takeC(struct C c);
void bvqp(s32 k, struct Q *p);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function bvqp         # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

	bl	k

	mov	r0, #0x6

# Reproduce asmlift on `divc100` — benchmark function synthetic:divc100:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:divc100:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	divc100
	.type	 divc100,function
	.thumb_func
divc100:
	push	{lr}
	mov	r1, #0x64
	bl	__divsi3
	pop	{r1}
	bx	r1
.Lfe1:
	.size	 divc100,.Lfe1-divc100
ASM_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name divc100          # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce m2c on `dvhome` — benchmark function synthetic:dvhome:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel dvhome
    stwu    r1,-16(r1)
    stw     r31,12(r1)
    lwz     r31,20(r3)
    li      r31,0
    stw     r31,0(r4)
    lwz     r31,12(r1)
    addi    r1,r1,16
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
void dvhome(s32 *p, s32 *q);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function dvhome       # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `dvhome` — benchmark function synthetic:dvhome:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# mwcc_242_81's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:dvhome:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

target.o:     file format elf32-powerpc


Disassembly of section .text:

00000000 <dvhome>:
   0:	stwu    r1,-16(r1)
   4:	stw     r31,12(r1)
   8:	lwz     r31,20(r3)
   c:	li      r31,0
  10:	stw     r31,0(r4)
  14:	lwz     r31,12(r1)
  18:	addi    r1,r1,16
  1c:	blr
ASM_INPUT

# The target object's objdump -s -r -t dump — the data sections (jump tables, anonymous
# constants) the text-only disassembly lacks; the benchmark recovered them from the object.
cat > dump.txt <<'DUMP_INPUT'

target.o:     file format elf32-powerpc

SYMBOL TABLE:
00000000 l    df *ABS*	00000000 ref.c
00000000 l    d  .text	00000000 .text
00000000 l    d  .mwcats.text	00000000 .mwcats.text
00000000 g     F .text	00000020 dvhome


RELOCATION RECORDS FOR [.mwcats.text]:
OFFSET   TYPE              VALUE
00000004 R_PPC_ADDR32      dvhome


Contents of section .text:
 0000 9421fff0 93e1000c 83e30014 3be00000  .!..........;...
 0010 93e40000 83e1000c 38210010 4e800020  ........8!..N.. 
Contents of section .mwcats.text:
 0000 02000020 00000000                    ... ....        
Contents of section .comment:
 0000 436f6465 57617272 696f720a 02040201  CodeWarrior.....
 0010 01020016 2c000000 00000000 00000000  ....,...........
 0020 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000  ................
 0030 00000000 00000001 00000000 00000004  ................
 0040 00000000 00000004 00000000 00000004  ................
 0050 00000000                             ....
DUMP_INPUT

# The prototypes the benchmark fed asmlift: its callees' arities, void-ness and declared types.
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "dvhome": {
    "params": [
      "s32 *",
      "s32 *"
    ],
    "returnsVoid": true,
    "paramNames": [
      "p",
      "q"
    ]
  }
}
PROTO_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name dvhome           # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `farjump_pool` — benchmark function synthetic:farjump_pool:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:farjump_pool:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

.text

	bl	__nesf2
	add	r1, r0, #0

int fcmpne(float,float);
CTX_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes AND the declarations of this row's authored symbol map. The synthetic tier measures
# COLD recovery and is symmetric by construction, so a row that hands asmlift a map hands m2c the
# same map: the block above is that map rendered to C by asmlift's own declaration renderer, not a
# second hand-written claim beside it. What the row measures is the reference SOURCE's spelling,
# which is in neither channel — see the asmlift script's --config for the map's own JSON.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
typedef unsigned char u8;typedef unsigned short u16;typedef unsigned int u32;typedef signed char s8;typedef short s16;typedef int s32;typedef long long s64;typedef unsigned long long u64;
struct Slots { u8 f[64]; };
extern struct Slots *gP;
void fnA(void);
void fnB(void);
struct Q { void *prev; void *cur; };
extern struct Q gQ;

void fnA(void); void fnB(void); void gcsearms(void);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target gba            # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function gcsearms     # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `gcsearms` — benchmark function synthetic:gcsearms:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH a symbol map, and unlike a real row's it is AUTHORED — the
# benchmark's synthetic dataset hand-writes it (apps/benchmark/dataset/synthetic.ts), because
# these rows exercise rules that only fire when a map declares a bitfield member, a sized
# pointer member or an array's rank, and there is no project ELF to derive one from. Step 1
# writes that same map next to target.o as symbols.json and names it in the generated
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), so this run loads exactly what the row was measured
# with. No checkout is involved.

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# It also writes this row's authored symbol map as symbols.json and names it in that
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), which is how the CLI loads the map the row was
# measured with.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:gcsearms:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

  },

  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name gcsearms         # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `gcsedup` — benchmark function synthetic:gcsedup:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH a symbol map, and unlike a real row's it is AUTHORED — the
# benchmark's synthetic dataset hand-writes it (apps/benchmark/dataset/synthetic.ts), because
# these rows exercise rules that only fire when a map declares a bitfield member, a sized
# pointer member or an array's rank, and there is no project ELF to derive one from. Step 1
# writes that same map next to target.o as symbols.json and names it in the generated
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), so this run loads exactly what the row was measured
# with. No checkout is involved.

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# It also writes this row's authored symbol map as symbols.json and names it in that
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), which is how the CLI loads the map the row was
# measured with.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:gcsedup:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# The exact agbcc `.s` text.

extern struct Slots *gP;

void fnB(void);

extern struct Q gQ;
void fnC(void);

void fnA(void); void fnB(void); void fnC(void); void gcseflat(void);
CTX_INPUT

)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s
scripts.asmlift:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `gcseflat` — benchmark function synthetic:gcseflat:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH a symbol map, and unlike a real row's it is AUTHORED — the
# benchmark's synthetic dataset hand-writes it (apps/benchmark/dataset/synthetic.ts), because
# these rows exercise rules that only fire when a map declares a bitfield member, a sized
# pointer member or an array's rank, and there is no project ELF to derive one from. Step 1
# writes that same map next to target.o as symbols.json and names it in the generated
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), so this run loads exactly what the row was measured
# with. No checkout is involved.

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# It also writes this row's authored symbol map as symbols.json and names it in that
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), which is how the CLI loads the map the row was
# measured with.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:gcseflat:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	gcseflat
	.type	 gcseflat,function
	.thumb_func

	ldr	r3, .L13
	ldr	r2, [r3]
	add	r0, r2, #0
	add	r0, r0, #0x37
	ldrb	r1, [r0]
	mov	r0, #0x80
	and	r0, r0, r1
	cmp	r0, #0
	beq	.L3	@cond_branch
	mov	r1, #0x0
	ldr	r4, .L13+0x4
	mov	r2, #0x0
.L7:
	ldr	r0, [r3]
	add	r0, r0, r1
	strb	r2, [r0]
	add	r0, r1, #0x1
	lsl	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsr	r1, r0, #0x18
	cmp	r1, #0x4
	bls	.L7	@cond_branch
	b	.L9
.L14:
	.align	2, 0
.L13:
	.word	gP
	.word	gQ
.L3:
	ldrb	r0, [r2, #0x8]
	cmp	r0, #0x7f
	bne	.L10	@cond_branch
	ldr	r1, .L15
	ldr	r0, .L15+0x4
	str	r0, [r1, #0x4]
	b	.L2
.L16:
	.align	2, 0
.L15:
	.word	gQ
	.word	fnA
.L10:
	ldrb	r0, [r2, #0x9]
	ldr	r4, .L17
	cmp	r0, #0x7f
	bne	.L9	@cond_branch
	ldr	r0, .L17+0x4
	b	.L12
.L18:
	.align	2, 0
.L17:
	.word	gQ
	.word	fnC
.L9:
	ldr	r0, .L19
.L12:

# The prototypes the benchmark fed asmlift: its callees' arities, void-ness and declared types.
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "gcseflat": {
    "returnsVoid": true
  },
  "fnA": {
    "params": 0,
    "returnsVoid": true
  },
  "fnB": {
    "params": 0,
    "returnsVoid": true
  },
  "fnC": {
    "params": 0,
    "returnsVoid": true
  }
}
PROTO_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name gcseflat         # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce m2c on `grv_add_r15` — benchmark function synthetic:grv_add_r15:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel grv_add_r15
    add     r3,r3,r15
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function grv_add_r15  # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce asmlift on `grv_add_r15` — benchmark function synthetic:grv_add_r15:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# mwcc_242_81's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:grv_add_r15:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

target.o:     file format elf32-powerpc


Disassembly of section .text:

00000000 <grv_add_r15>:
   0:	add     r3,r3,r15
   4:	blr
ASM_INPUT

# The target object's objdump -s -r -t dump — the data sections (jump tables, anonymous
# constants) the text-only disassembly lacks; the benchmark recovered them from the object.
cat > dump.txt <<'DUMP_INPUT'

target.o:     file format elf32-powerpc

SYMBOL TABLE:
00000000 l    df *ABS*	00000000 ref.c
00000000 l    d  .text	00000000 .text
00000000 l    d  .sbss	00000000 .sbss
00000000 l    d  .mwcats.text	00000000 .mwcats.text
00000000 g     O .sbss	00000004 g
00000000 g     F .text	00000008 grv_add_r15
00000004 g     O .sbss	00000004 g0


RELOCATION RECORDS FOR [.mwcats.text]:
OFFSET   TYPE              VALUE
00000004 R_PPC_ADDR32      grv_add_r15


Contents of section .text:
 0000 7c637a14 4e800020                    |cz.N..         
Contents of section .mwcats.text:
 0000 02000008 00000000                    ........        
Contents of section .comment:
 0000 436f6465 57617272 696f720a 02040201  CodeWarrior.....
 0010 01020016 2c040000 00000000 00000000  ....,...........
 0020 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000  ................
 0030 00000000 00000001 00000000 00000004  ................
 0040 00000000 00000008 00000000 00000004  ................
 0050 00000000 00000004 00000000 00000004  ................
 0060 00000000 00000004 00000000           ............
DUMP_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name grv_add_r15      # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce m2c on `grv_stkargw_s0` — benchmark function synthetic:grv_stkargw_s0:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel grv_stkargw_s0
    addiu	$sp, $sp, -32
    move	$s0, $a0
    li	$a0, 1
    li	$a1, 2
    li	$a2, 3
    li	$a3, 4
    sw	$ra, 24($sp)
    jal	k
    sw	$s0, 16($sp)
    lw	$ra, 24($sp)
    jr	$ra
    addiu	$sp, $sp, 32
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
int k(int,int,int,int,int);
void grv_stkargw_s0(int);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function grv_stkargw_s0 # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

results.note: the `||` at `ifand_far`'s distance. The long branch INVERTS the last test, which moves the shared arm to the other successor slot — so a long `||` stamps the same pair (`scSharedOnFall` false, `scSharedIsTaken` true) as a SHORT `&&` and wants the opposite spelling. Two booleans cannot separate them; the third stamp `scEdgeRelayed` is what does, and this is the only row whose SPELLING that stamp decides — the corpus carries 9 other stamped sites, all MIPS rows where no ±256-byte range exists and none is a sense site (packages/core/test/site-sense.test.ts pins the cell). Like `ifand_far` its SCORE referees nothing: it MATCHes on `/flip-join` whichever way the fold spelled the site. Nor does the FAN carry the variation here: measured, the row enumerates 4 candidates and no `/site-sense` at all, because at one site the variation re-spells what `/flip-join` already spelled and the tree dedup drops the duplicate. A named row the fan never enumerates is worth saying out loud

set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The exact agbcc `.s` text the benchmark fed m2c, verbatim.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	ifor_near
	.type	 ifor_near,function
	.thumb_func
ifor_near:
	cmp	r0, #0
	bne	.L4	@cond_branch
	cmp	r1, #0
	beq	.L3	@cond_branch
.L4:
	mov	r0, #0x1
	str	r0, [r2]
	mov	r0, #0x2
	str	r0, [r3]
	mov	r0, #0x3
	str	r0, [r2, #0x4]
	mov	r0, #0x4
	str	r0, [r3, #0x4]
	b	.L5
.L3:
	mov	r0, #0x1
	neg	r0, r0
	str	r0, [r2]
.L5:
	ldr	r0, [r2, #0x4]
	bx	lr
.Lfe1:
	.size	 ifor_near,.Lfe1-ifor_near
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.

# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'

args=(
  --target gba            # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function ifor_near    # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce asmlift on `jt_rndjoin` — benchmark function synthetic:jt_rndjoin:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:jt_rndjoin:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

  --name jt_rndjoin       # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1

# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH a symbol map, and unlike a real row's it is AUTHORED — the
# benchmark's synthetic dataset hand-writes it (apps/benchmark/dataset/synthetic.ts), because
# these rows exercise rules that only fire when a map declares a bitfield member, a sized
# pointer member or an array's rank, and there is no project ELF to derive one from. Step 1
# writes that same map next to target.o as symbols.json and names it in the generated
# decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.symbols), so this run loads exactly what the row was measured

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `llshl` — benchmark function synthetic:llshl:ido7.1.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel llshl
    addiu	$sp, $sp, -24
    sw	$ra, 20($sp)
    sw	$a2, 32($sp)
    move	$a3, $a2
    sra	$a2, $a2, 0x1f
    sw	$a0, 24($sp)
    jal	__ll_lshift
    sw	$a1, 28($sp)
    lw	$ra, 20($sp)
    addiu	$sp, $sp, 24
    jr	$ra
    nop
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target mips-ido-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function llshl        # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `maxi` — benchmark function synthetic:maxi:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel maxi
    cmpw    r3,r4
    ble-     .Lc
    mr      r4,r3
.Lc:
    mr      r3,r4
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function maxi         # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce m2c on `mergeif` — benchmark function synthetic:mergeif:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel mergeif
    lw	$a2, 0($a1)
    slti	$v0, $a2, 32
    beqz	$v0, .L14
    li	$v1, 32
    move	$v1, $a2
.L14:
    lw	$a3, 4($a1)
    slti	$v0, $a3, 32
    beqz	$v0, .L28
    li	$a2, 32
    move	$a2, $a3
.L28:
    andi	$v0, $a0, 0x1
    beqz	$v0, .L48
    nop
    lw	$a2, 8($a1)
    nor	$v0, $zero, $a2
    sra	$v0, $v0, 0x1f
    j	.L58
    and	$a2, $a2, $v0
.L48:
    lw	$v1, 12($a1)
    nor	$v0, $zero, $v1
    sra	$v0, $v0, 0x1f
    and	$v1, $v1, $v0
.L58:
    sll	$v0, $v1, 0x2
    addu	$v0, $v0, $v1
    sll	$v0, $v0, 0x1
    jr	$ra
    addu	$v0, $v0, $a2
    nop
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function mergeif      # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce asmlift on `offhome` — benchmark function synthetic:offhome:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:offhome:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	offhome
	.type	 offhome,function
	.thumb_func
offhome:
	push	{r4, r5, r6, lr}
	add	r6, r1, #0
	bl	getbuf
	add	r5, r0, #0x4
	mov	r4, #0x0
	cmp	r4, r6
	bge	.L4	@cond_branch
.L6:
	add	r0, r5, r4
	ldrb	r0, [r0]
	bl	sink
	add	r4, r4, #0x1
	cmp	r4, r6
	blt	.L6	@cond_branch
.L4:
	sub	r0, r5, #0x4
	bl	putbuf
	pop	{r4, r5, r6}
	pop	{r0}
	bx	r0
.Lfe1:
	.size	 offhome,.Lfe1-offhome
ASM_INPUT

# The prototypes the benchmark fed asmlift: its callees' arities, void-ness and declared types.
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "getbuf": {
    "params": 1
  },
  "putbuf": {
    "params": 1,
    "returnsVoid": true
  },
  "sink": {
    "params": 1,
    "returnsVoid": true
  },
  "offhome": {
    "returnsVoid": true,
    "paramNames": [
      "k",
      "n"
    ]
  }
}
PROTO_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name offhome          # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce asmlift on `retchain` — benchmark function synthetic:retchain:gcc2.7.2.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `savechain` — benchmark function synthetic:savechain:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel savechain
    stwu    r1,-32(r1)
    mflr    r0
    stw     r0,36(r1)
    addi    r11,r1,32
    bl       _savegpr_27
    mr      r27,r4
    mr      r28,r5
    mr      r29,r6
    mr      r30,r7
    mr      r31,r8
    bl       k
    add     r3,r27,r3
    bl       k
    add     r3,r28,r3
    bl       k
    add     r3,r29,r3
    bl       k
    add     r3,r30,r3
    bl       k
    add     r3,r31,r3
    addi    r11,r1,32
    bl       _restgpr_27
    lwz     r0,36(r1)
    mtlr    r0
    addi    r1,r1,32
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
int k(int);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function savechain    # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce m2c on `sfar_msg` — benchmark function synthetic:sfar_msg:mwcc_233_163n.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel sfar_msg
    lbz     r0,0(r4)
    addis   r3,r3,1
    stb     r0,2596(r3)
    lwz     r3,2600(r3)
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
struct Play; s32 sfar_msg(struct Play*,u8*);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function sfar_msg     # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce m2c on `sfield` — benchmark function synthetic:sfield:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The exact agbcc `.s` text the benchmark fed m2c, verbatim.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	sfield
	.type	 sfield,function
	.thumb_func
sfield:
	ldr	r0, [r0, #0x4]
	bx	lr
.Lfe1:
	.size	 sfield,.Lfe1-sfield
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target gba            # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function sfield       # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s
scripts.asmlift:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `sfield` — benchmark function synthetic:sfield:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:sfield:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	sfield
	.type	 sfield,function
	.thumb_func
sfield:
	ldr	r0, [r0, #0x4]
	bx	lr
.Lfe1:
	.size	 sfield,.Lfe1-sfield
ASM_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name sfield           # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce m2c on `sret8` — benchmark function synthetic:sret8:gcc2.7.2.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel sret8
    addiu	$sp, $sp, -32
    sw	$ra, 24($sp)
    move	$a1, $a0
    jal	mk8
    addiu	$a0, $sp, 16
    lw	$v0, 16($sp)
    lui	$at, %hi(gW)
    sw	$v0, %lo(gW)($at)
    lw	$v0, 20($sp)
    lui	$at, %hi(gW2)
    sw	$v0, %lo(gW2)($at)
    lw	$ra, 24($sp)
    jr	$ra
    addiu	$sp, $sp, 32
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
struct S8 { u32 a, b; };
struct S8 mk8(s32 x);
void sret8(s32 x);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function sret8        # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `sret8` — benchmark function synthetic:sret8:gcc2.7.2.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# gcc2.7.2's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:sret8:gcc2.7.2 --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

  10:	addiu	a0,sp,16
  14:	lw	v0,16(sp)
  18:	lui	at,0x0
  1c:	sw	v0,0(at)
  20:	lw	v0,20(sp)
  24:	lui	at,0x0
  28:	sw	v0,0(at)
  2c:	lw	ra,24(sp)
  30:	jr	ra
  34:	addiu	sp,sp,32
	...

# constants) the text-only disassembly lacks; the benchmark recovered them from the object.

00000000 l    d  .bss	00000000 .bss
00000000 l    d  .reginfo	00000000 .reginfo
00000000 l    d  .note	00000000 .note
00000000 l    d  .comment	00000000 .comment
00000000 g     F .text	00000038 sret8
00000000         *UND*	00000000 mk8
00000000         *UND*	00000000 gW

0000000c R_MIPS_26         mk8

0000001c R_MIPS_LO16       gW
00000024 R_MIPS_HI16       gW2
00000028 R_MIPS_LO16       gW2


Contents of section .text:

 0010 27a40010 8fa20010 3c010000 ac220000  '.......<...."..
 0020 8fa20014 3c010000 ac220000 8fbf0018  ....<...."......
 0030 03e00008 27bd0020 00000000 00000000  ....'.. ........
Contents of section .reginfo:
 0000 a0000036 00000000 00000000 00000000  ...6............

Contents of section .note:

 0010 31000000                             1...            
Contents of section .comment:

 0010 3200                                 2.

# The prototypes the benchmark fed asmlift: its callees' arities, void-ness and declared types.
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "mk8": {
    "params": [
      "s32"

      "kind": "struct",

  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target gcc2.7.2       # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name sret8            # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.

# Reproduce m2c on `sretbf` — benchmark function synthetic:sretbf:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel sretbf
    stwu    r1,-16(r1)
    mflr    r0
    stw     r0,20(r1)
    bl       mkbf
    stw     r3,8(r1)
    lbz     r0,8(r1)
    clrlwi  r0,r0,28
    stw     r0,gW@sda21(r13)
    lwz     r0,20(r1)
    mtlr    r0
    addi    r1,r1,16
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
struct Bf { u32 a : 4; u32 b : 4; };
struct Bf mkbf(s32 x);
void sretbf(s32 x);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function sretbf       # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `sumto` — benchmark function synthetic:sumto:ido7.1.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel sumto
    move	$v1, $zero
    blez	$a0, .L54
    move	$v0, $zero
    andi	$a2, $a0, 0x3
    beqz	$a2, .L30
    move	$a1, $a2
    addu	$v1, $v1, $v0
.L1c:
    addiu	$v0, $v0, 1
    bnel	$a1, $v0, .L1c
    addu	$v1, $v1, $v0
    beq	$v0, $a0, .L54
    nop
.L30:
    addu	$v1, $v1, $v0
    addu	$v1, $v1, $v0
    addiu	$v1, $v1, 1
    addu	$v1, $v1, $v0
    addiu	$v1, $v1, 2
    addu	$v1, $v1, $v0
    addiu	$v0, $v0, 4
    bne	$v0, $a0, .L30
    addiu	$v1, $v1, 3
.L54:
    jr	$ra
    move	$v0, $v1
    nop
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target mips-ido-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function sumto        # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `sw_forjt_u32` — benchmark function synthetic:sw_forjt_u32:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# gcc2.7.2kmc's canonical flags.

pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:sw_forjt_u32:gcc2.7.2kmc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# Reproduce asmlift on `sw_gotocase_inner` — benchmark function synthetic:sw_gotocase_inner:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):

# mwcc_242_81's canonical flags.

set -euo pipefail

# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;

ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `sw_xjret_end` — benchmark function synthetic:sw_xjret_end:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# agbcc's canonical flags.

pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:sw_xjret_end:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# Reproduce asmlift on `sw_xjret_end` — benchmark function synthetic:sw_xjret_end:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# Reproduce asmlift on `sw_xjret` — benchmark function synthetic:sw_xjret:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:sw_xjret:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name sw_xjret         # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.

extern s32 gOut;
extern s32 gLo, gHi;

  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function sw_xjret     # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a

# Reproduce m2c on `thrwalkba` — benchmark function synthetic:thrwalkba:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel thrwalkba
    lui	$v1, %hi(gTbl)
    addiu	$v1, $v1, %lo(gTbl)
    addiu	$a2, $v1, 12
    sltu	$v0, $v1, $a2
    beqz	$v0, .L40
    nop
    andi	$a1, $a0, 0xff
.L1c:
    lbu	$v0, 1($v1)
    beq	$a1, $v0, .L40
    nop
    lbu	$v0, 0($v1)
    beq	$a1, $v0, .L50
    addiu	$v1, $v1, 4
    sltu	$v0, $v1, $a2
    bnez	$v0, .L1c
    nop
.L40:
    lbu	$v1, 0($v1)
    andi	$v0, $a0, 0xff
    bne	$v0, $v1, .L54
    li	$v0, 2
.L50:
    li	$v0, 1
.L54:
    lui	$at, %hi(gOut)
    jr	$ra
    sb	$v0, %lo(gOut)($at)
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
void thrwalkba(u8 x);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function thrwalkba    # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce asmlift on `ubyte` — benchmark function synthetic:ubyte:ido7.1.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# ido7.1's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:ubyte:ido7.1 --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `ubyte` — benchmark function synthetic:ubyte:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel ubyte
    stw     r4,0(r3)
    lbzx    r3,r3,r5
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function ubyte        # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel uninit_saved
    addiu	$sp, $sp, -40
    sw	$s3, 28($sp)
    lw	$s3, 56($sp)
    sw	$s4, 32($sp)
    lw	$s4, 60($sp)
    sw	$s0, 16($sp)
    move	$s0, $a2
    sw	$s1, 20($sp)
    move	$s1, $a3
    sw	$ra, 36($sp)
    beqz	$a0, .L3c
    sw	$s2, 24($sp)
    jal	k
    move	$a0, $a1
    move	$s2, $v0
.L3c:
    jal	k
    move	$a0, $s0
    jal	k
    addu	$a0, $v0, $s1
    jal	k
    addu	$a0, $v0, $s3
    jal	k
    addu	$a0, $v0, $s4
    addu	$v0, $v0, $s2
    lw	$ra, 36($sp)
    lw	$s4, 32($sp)
    lw	$s3, 28($sp)
    lw	$s2, 24($sp)
    lw	$s1, 20($sp)
    lw	$s0, 16($sp)
    jr	$ra
    addiu	$sp, $sp, 40

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `upd_scpy` — benchmark function synthetic:upd_scpy:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel upd_scpy
    lbu	$v0, 0($a1)
    beqz	$v0, .L20
    sb	$v0, 0($a0)
.Lc:
    addiu	$a1, $a1, 1
    lbu	$v0, 0($a1)
    addiu	$a0, $a0, 1
    bnez	$v0, .Lc
    sb	$v0, 0($a0)
.L20:
    jr	$ra
    nop
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
void upd_scpy(u8 *d, u8 *s);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function upd_scpy     # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The exact agbcc `.s` text the benchmark fed m2c, verbatim.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	zxparam
	.type	 zxparam,function
	.thumb_func
zxparam:
	push	{r4, lr}
	lsl	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsr	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsl	r1, r1, #0x18
	lsr	r1, r1, #0x18
	mov	r4, #0x1
	add	r3, r0, #0
	and	r3, r3, r4
	str	r3, [r2]
	add	r3, r1, #0
	and	r3, r3, r4
	str	r3, [r2, #0x4]
	add	r0, r0, r1
	str	r0, [r2, #0x8]
	pop	{r4}
	pop	{r0}
	bx	r0
.Lfe1:
	.size	 zxparam,.Lfe1-zxparam
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
void zxparam(u8 a, u8 b, s32 *out);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target gba            # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function zxparam      # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s
scripts.asmlift:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `zxparam` — benchmark function synthetic:zxparam:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:zxparam:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	zxparam
	.type	 zxparam,function
	.thumb_func
zxparam:
	push	{r4, lr}
	lsl	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsr	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsl	r1, r1, #0x18
	lsr	r1, r1, #0x18
	mov	r4, #0x1
	add	r3, r0, #0
	and	r3, r3, r4
	str	r3, [r2]
	add	r3, r1, #0
	and	r3, r3, r4
	str	r3, [r2, #0x4]
	add	r0, r0, r1
	str	r0, [r2, #0x8]
	pop	{r4}
	pop	{r0}
	bx	r0
.Lfe1:
	.size	 zxparam,.Lfe1-zxparam
ASM_INPUT

# The prototypes the benchmark fed asmlift: its callees' arities, void-ness and declared types.
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "zxparam": {
    "params": [
      "u8",
      "u8",
      "s32 *"
    ],
    "returnsVoid": true,
    "paramNames": [
      "a",
      "b",
      "out"
    ]
  }
}
PROTO_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name zxparam          # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"
